answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance comes from forcing each identity to grow a unique crystal of interaction entropy by answering a continuous zephyr of randomized peer probes that ripple across the ocean of live agent traffic. An attacker must pay linear time and compute for every fake identity so that its crystal stays statistically independent; any correlation cluster is automatically down-weighted or slashed, making large farms far more expensive than honest single agents who incur only ordinary participation cost.
